# **Using Kiro at Appian: A Guide for Product & Design**

Welcome to Kiro, your personal AI partner designed to supercharge how we build products at Appian. Whether you are a Product Manager defining a new feature or a UX Designer prototyping a flow, Kiro helps you translate your ideas into actionable plans¯ and documentation.

## **1\. Getting Access**

Before you can use Kiro, you need a business license to access our private codebase.

* **Who can sign up?** Anyone in Appian Product, Engineering, or Infosec.  
* **How to request a license:** You may already have a license. Go ahead and download Kiro and try to log in. If you get an error, reach out to your **GDL** or your **SBU Head** (Product, Quality, or Dev).  
* **The Wait Period:** After your access is granted, it typically takes **one business day** for your account to sync with our security systems (Okta).

## **2\. Choosing Your Tool: The Kiro IDE**

While engineers often use a text-only interface (the CLI), we highly recommend the **Kiro IDE** for Product and Design roles.

The Kiro IDE is a dedicated workspace where you can "vibe code"—quickly prototyping ideas and generating high-quality specifications using natural language. 

### **Pre-Setup Instructions** \- if you don’t typically write code, you may need to install some tools

**Mac**

1. Open **Terminal**.  
2. Check if Xcode Command Line Tools are installed on your machine using the command *xcode-select \-p*  
   1. If they are, you should see the path at which they are installed  
   2. If they are not, you’ll receive an error. Install them using the command *xcode-select \--install*  
3. Use command: brew \-v to see if Homebrew is installed. If it is, move to step 4  
   1. If you have brew installed, run *brew update* to ensure you are on a version that supports Kiro.  
   2. If you do not have brew installed, navigate to the Homebrew [site](https://brew.sh/) and copy the install homebrew script (You may be prompted for a password, if you are, use the same password to log into your computer. You won’t see your password when you type it in.)  
      1. Paste the script in Terminal and press enter  
      2. If you have an M1, M2, M3, or M4 Mac, you must manually add Homebrew to your system's path. After the script finishes, look for the "Next steps" section in the Terminal output. It will provide two or three commands similar to these (run them **exactly as shown in your terminal**):

```shell
(echo; echo 'eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"') >> ~/.zprofile
eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"

```

      3. To ensure everything is set up correctly, run *brew doctor*. If successful, it will return: *Your system is ready to brew*.  
4. Install **uv** using Terminal command: *brew install uv*

**Windows**

1. Open **PowerShell** as Administrator (right-click PowerShell and select "Run as administrator").  
2. Check if Windows development tools are available by running: *git \--version*  
   1. If you see a version number, you have Git installed and can proceed to step 4  
   2. If you get an error, continue to step 3  
3. Install Git for Windows:  
   1. Download from [https://git-scm.com/download/win](https://git-scm.com/download/win)  
   2. Run the installer and use the default settings  
4. Check if you have a package manager installed by running: *winget \--version*  
   1. If you see a version number, proceed to step 5  
   2. If you get an error, winget should be pre-installed on Windows 10 (version 1809+) and Windows 11\. Try updating Windows or install it from the Microsoft Store (search for "App Installer")  
5. Install uv using PowerShell command: *winget install \--id=astral-sh.uv \-e*  
6. Close and reopen PowerShell to ensure the uv command is available  
7. Note: After installation, verify uv is working by running: *uv \--version*

## **SSH Authentication Setup**

Before cloning, you must link your computer to GitLab. Follow these steps based on your operating system.

### **1\. Check for an existing key**

Open your terminal (**Terminal** on Mac, **PowerShell** or **Git Bash** on Windows) and run:

* **Mac/PC:** ls \-al \~/.ssh

If you see id\_ed25519.pub or id\_rsa.pub, you already have a key. **Skip to Step 3\.**

### **2\. Generate a new key (if needed)**

If the folder was empty, run the following (replacing the email with your own):

* **Mac/PC:** ssh-keygen \-t ed25519 \-C "your\_email@example.com"  
* *Action:* Press **Enter** to accept the default file location. Choose a passphrase (recommended) or leave it blank.

### **3\. Add key to the SSH Agent**

This ensures your computer uses the key when you run the git clone command:

* **On macOS:**  
  * Start agent: eval "$(ssh-agent \-s)"  
  * Add key: ssh-add \--apple-use-keychain \~/.ssh/id\_ed25519 (Use id\_rsa if that was your filename in Step 1\)  
* **On Windows (Git Bash):**  
  * Start agent: eval "$(ssh-agent \-s)"  
  * Add key: ssh-add \~/.ssh/id\_ed25519 (Use id\_rsa if that was your filename in Step 1\)

### **4\. Link the Public Key to GitLab (if needed)**

You only need to perform this step if you didn’t already have an SSH key in Step 1 above. You must now "handshake" with the server by providing your public key. 

* **Copy your key to the clipboard:**  
  1. **Mac:** pbcopy \< \~/.ssh/id\_ed25519.pub (Use id\_rsa if that was your filename in Step 1\)  
  2. **Windows (Git Bash):** cat  \~/.ssh/id\_ed25519.pub | clip (Use id\_rsa if that was your filename in Step 1\)  
* **Add to GitLab:**  
  1. Log in to [gitlab.appian-stratus.com](http://gitlab.appian-stratus.com).  
  2. Click your **Avatar** (top right) \> **Edit Profile**.  
  3. On the left sidebar, select **SSH Keys**.  
  4. Click **Add new key**, paste your code, and save.

## **3\. Common Tasks for Product & Design**

Kiro uses simple "slash commands" to help you work. Type these directly into the chat panel:

| Command | Best Use Case for PMs & Designers |
| :---- | :---- |
| /dev | **Feature Planning:** Ask Kiro to create a step-by-step implementation plan for a new feature idea. |
| /doc | **Documentation:** Use this to automatically generate READMEs or project documentation based on your notes. |
| /help | **Guidance:** Provides an overview of everything Kiro can do and examples of questions you can ask. |
| /clear | **Fresh Start:** Clears the current conversation so you can start a new topic without old context interfering. |

## **4\. Connecting your Google Workspace CLI**

This connects Kiro to your Google Drive, Gmail, Calendar, etc. allowing Kiro to read your docs and manage your schedule.

**Mac Installation Instructions in Terminal**

1. (If you don’t have it) Install python3

   `brew install python3`

2. Install Google Workspace CLI

   	brew  install  googleworkspace-cli

3. Clone the dotfiles [repo](https://gitlab.appian-stratus.com/medhat.galal/dotfiles). 

   1. Navigate to your preferred folder in Terminal (some of us have a repo folder) and paste the git clone command.

      `git clone git@gitlab.appian-stratus.com:medhat.galal/dotfiles.git ~/Repo/dotfiles 2>&1`

4. CD into the dotfiles repo.

   `cd ~/Repo/dotfiles`

   

5. Run two dotfiles commands. The first one gets a token that you need for the second command. After each command you need to select your preferred editor style (vim or emacs, I picked **vim**) and approve a high-risk action ensure.secrets \- **yes**.

   `./dotfiles converge --intent "install" --interactive`

   

   `./dotfiles converge --apply --approval-token [your token here from the previous command] --interactive`

6. Click through the prompts to give Google Workspace permissions. 

7. If you run into this error: "error\[auth\]: No OAuth client configured", make sure that the following line is uncommented in \~/.secrets.env:

   `export GOOGLE_CLOUD_SHARED_SECRETS_PROJECT="peng-os"`

8. Authenticate your Google Workspace Services. Select either a or b.

   1. Auto-select Drive, Gmail, Calendar, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Tasks, and Chat

   `gws auth login -s drive,gmail,calendar,docs,sheets,slides,tasks,chat`

   2. View the entire list of services and select the ones you want

`gws auth login` 

9. Press enter to confirm all of the services, and copy and paste the link to Chrome to finish authenticating.  
10. Download [this steering file](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1PRBAPir2nhvctPxiooNT3Va745GsHa2Q/view?usp=drive_link) and add it to your .kiro/steering folder at the hierarchy level that best suits your use case. I put mine in the topmost folder, so I can use it for all my Kiro projects.  
    1. Tip: To view hidden folders like .kiro, use keyboard shortcut **CMD \+ SHIFT \+ .** 

See [Troubleshooting](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1utoj31oMmKbLrIECvAA1-sGC0u1nPM6U8cYUfkm4_1U/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.fp06tp4sj8u9)	for additional troubleshooting with installing the Google Workspace

### **What can you do now?**

* **Summarize Meetings:** *"Check my calendar for tomorrow and draft a list of follow-up items for my 10 AM meeting."*  
* **Analyze Specs:** *"Read my 'Product Spec' doc in Google Drive and summarize the open questions."*  
* **Automate Reporting:** *"Search my Gmail for 'UI Feedback' threads from this week and create a summary report."*  
* **Capacity Planning:** *"Ingest my Google Doc on 'Project Alpha' and help me generate SWAG estimates for capacity planning."*

## **5\. Guidelines for Success**

* **You are the boss:** Kiro is an eager assistant, but it lacks your domain knowledge. You are responsible for the final quality.  
* **Be specific:** If you aren’t sure what you want to accomplish, Kiro won't either. Provide clear goals.  
* **Keep it short:** AI works best when solving one problem at a time. If a conversation gets too long, use /clear to start fresh. You can also create a new chat session with a clean context by clicking the **\+** at the top of the chat panel.

## **6\. Troubleshooting**

* **"Access Denied":** This usually means your account is still syncing. Wait one full business day after being granted access.  
* **Port in Use (Error 8000):** If Kiro says "Port is already in use," it's likely a background process. Restarting your computer usually fixes this.  
* **Google Connection Failed:** If Google tools aren't working, go back to the **MCP Servers** tab and check if the status light is green. If not, click "Reconnect."
